title: Bioreactors & Tissue Culture Engineering
description: Scale cell culture and tissue maturation through mass transfer, shear, process monitoring, control, sterility, and design-of-experiments principles.

outcomes.description: Interpret growth kinetics and process data.
Design controls and acceptance criteria for a reproducible process.

lesson_objectives.description: Fit a simple exponential growth model over its valid phase.
Calculate doubling time and identify when exponential assumptions fail.
Compare oxygen transfer capacity to cellular demand.
Estimate Reynolds number and mixing-time tradeoffs.
Use dimensionless similarity only when the relevant constraints are preserved.
Choose critical process parameters and quality attributes.
Separate process drift from assay variation.

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

modules.title: Growth kinetics and process mass balance

lessons.title: Growth kinetics and process mass balance
lessons.worked_example: If viable cell count rises from 0.5 to 2 million cells/mL over 48 h in log phase, μ=ln(4)/48=0.0289 h⁻¹ and doubling time is 24 h.

lessons.title: Oxygen transfer and consumption
lessons.worked_example: If kLa=20 h⁻¹, C*=0.20 mM, and C=0.05 mM, OTR=3 mM/h in the simplified bulk model.

lessons.title: Mixing, shear, and scale-up
lessons.worked_example: Maintaining constant tip speed while increasing impeller diameter changes rotational speed and may alter mixing and power density; the chosen criterion must match the process limitation.

lessons.title: Process monitoring, control, and quality
lessons.worked_example: A dissolved-oxygen probe that drifts low can trigger excessive agitation; a second calibrated measurement or reference check can distinguish sensor drift from true oxygen limitation.
